test2_uaPoolSustained.purpose: Test whether any UA in production pool gets blocked by Cloudflare on sustained walk (8 pages x 5 UAs = 40 requests).
test2_uaPoolSustained.method: Walk /collection/ pages 1-8 with 5 distinct UAs (desktop-chrome, iphone-safari, mac-safari, linux-chrome, android-chrome), 800ms delay each.
test2_uaPoolSustained.verdict: 40/40 = 200 across all 5 UAs. No 'Just a moment' challenge body. No 403/503/429. iPhone UA is NOT load-bearing. Cloudflare is passive (cf-ray headers present per R1) but does NOT gate the crawler. hasWaf=false is operationally correct; DB's hasWaf=true + iPhone UA workaround is a defensive position that current evidence does not support.

test3_perPageTiming.purpose: Side-by-side timing perPage=100 vs perPage=24 at scale (skill anti-pattern: any 'X is faster' needs side-by-side timing).
test3_perPageTiming.method: 5 pages of /collection/ at each perPage, same UA, same delay.
test3_perPageTiming.verdict: Per-request latency identical (~280ms, 1.8% difference, noise). perPage=100 yields 4.17x more products per request. For 2706-product walk: p100 approximately 28 requests vs p24 approximately 113 requests - 75% fewer requests at same latency. perPage=100 wins decisively. R1 candidate correct, DB value 24 is suboptimal.

test4_dbExtraUrls.purpose: Test R1's Rule-C-violating exclusion of DB URLs the candidate dropped.
test4_dbExtraUrls.method: Direct GET each URL with ?limit=100, iPhone UA, 800ms delay.
test4_dbExtraUrls.verdict: All 4 URLs productive. /sale/hunting-super-specials/new-used-guns/ (31 products) likely overlaps /firearms/* leaves (same product slugs in sample) - include for safety, dedup handles overlap. /previously-owned-merchandise/ near-empty (1 product, non-firearm). /archery/* is scope choice (Rule C exclusion arguable). R1 dropping /sale/new-used-guns/ violated Rule C (no full-walk dedup proof); DB is right to include.
